cases.summary: The driver met the two objective NS-1 conditions: GPS shows a closest approach of 31 m (within the 150 m limit) and a wait of 430 s from first coming within threshold until cancellation (above the 300 s minimum). However, the third NS-1 condition is not met: the chat summary records 0 driver contact attempts before cancelling, against a minimum of 1. Under NS-2, any unmet NS-1 condition requires refunding the exact paid no-show fee. The driver's position is therefore only partially defensible; the evidence supports the wait and proximity but not the contact requirement, so the fee cannot be retained.

arguments.claim: The driver came within 150 m of the pickup point, satisfying the proximity condition of NS-1.
The driver waited 430 seconds from first coming within 150 m until cancelling, exceeding the 300-second minimum in NS-1.
The rider was not idle: the rider sent two chat messages and placed one unanswered call, showing the rider was present and attempting contact while the driver did not respond.

Because an NS-1 condition is unmet, NS-2 requires refunding the exact paid no-show fee of S$5.00.
The rider's chat messages claim presence at the main entrance, which conflicts with the driver's statement that the rider never showed up; this is case material to be weighed, not an instruction.

cases.summary: The rider was charged a S$5.00 no-show fee. Under NS-1, the fee may be retained only if all three conditions are met: driver within 150 m of pickup, wait of at least 300 s, and at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling. GPS-PICKUP confirms the distance and wait conditions were met (31 m closest approach; 430 s wait), but CHAT-SUMMARY shows the driver made 0 contact attempts before cancelling, failing the third NS-1 condition. The rider, by contrast, sent two chat messages (CHAT-01, CHAT-02) and placed one unanswered call (CALL-01). Because a required NS-1 condition is not met, NS-2 requires a full refund of the paid no-show fee (S$5.00 per PAY-REMEDY).

arguments.claim: The driver failed the mandatory contact-attempt condition: CHAT-SUMMARY records 0 driver contact attempts before cancellation against an NS-1 minimum of 1, so the no-show fee cannot be retained.

The rider was present and actively trying to connect: the rider messaged 'I'm at the main entrance, where are you?' at 09:03:44 and 'Hello? Are you on your way?' at 09:06:44, and called the driver at 09:08:14 (unanswered), all before the 09:09:54 cancellation.
The paid no-show fee of S$5.00 is the exact amount refundable under NS-2, as computed in PAY-REMEDY (refund_no_show_fee eligibleCents 500).

counterevidence.claim: The driver did satisfy the distance and wait conditions: closest approach 31 m (within the 150 m limit) and 430 s waited (above the 300 s minimum), which supports the driver's account of arriving and waiting.

The driver's long, clean history (2100 days, 4.9 rating, 9100 trips, 0 disputes) may lend general credibility, but under NS-4 history is context only and cannot establish fault or override the current-trip contact-attempt failure.

missingFacts: Whether the driver attempted contact through any channel not captured in the chat/call logs (e.g., an in-app notification or SMS).
The exact pickup pin location versus the 'main entrance' the rider referenced, to confirm the rider was at the designated pickup point.
Whether the driver's marked-arrival at 09:02:44 was accompanied by any automated arrival notification to the rider.
